e-10906.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Makes a Set Linearly Dependent
e-10906.problem:
The set $\{ \mathbf{a_1},\mathbf{a_2} \}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be $\mathbf{a}_2$ if
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083176/assets/2fc772925dd6b793bdcb3a1eca96ea7e7f5fed17425f3500638340e047170c60.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083176/assets/f73258610652de9a656f3c4ed202241c58c98f18391b1393dabe62d92d9bef7d.png)
e-10906.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_2$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{v}_1 + x_2 \mathbf{v}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

is $x_1 = x_2 = 0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083176/assets/210a5c50467861cdfe48b46f2098212bbf387270b420a05394e318a0e0b48c74.png)
To see why, notice that 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083176/assets/91a29b57d32ed8c8e702f2988f7714ffc343ed6b4707b86b49b708ffad5c8bc8.png)
In other words, the vectors $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are parallel.

To see why this means that $\mathbf a_1$ and $\mathbf a_2$ are linearly dependent, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation

$$
x_1 \mathbf{a}_1  +x_2  \mathbf{a}_2 = \mathbf{0}
$$

has the solution $x_1=\dfrac 1 3$ and $x_2=-1,$ which is different from $x_1=x_2=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=(-2)[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=-2{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}-2{a}_{1} & =0 \\ 2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

Question 1

The set {a1,a2} is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be a2 if a1=[51−2]?

a
[−2−104]
b
[4−2−10]
c
[−10−42]
d
[1024]
e
[−10−24]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We say that two vectors v1 and v2 are linearly independent if the only solution to the equation x1v1+x2v2=0 is x1=x2=0. Otherwise, the vectors are linearly dependent.

A set containing only two vectors is linearly dependent if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is a2=[−10−24]. To see why, notice that [−10−24]=(−2)[51−2]=−2a1. This way, we have 2a1−2a1=02a1+a2=0

In other words, the vectors a1 and a2 are parallel.

To see why this means that a1 and a2 are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

x1a1+x2a2=0

has the solution x1=2 and x2=1, which is different from x1=x2=0. Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Makes a Set Linearly Dependent
content.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]=(-2)[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=-2{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2{a}_{1}-2{a}_{1} & =0 \\ 2{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 15\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 15\end{aligned}]=-3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=-3{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}-3{a}_{1} & =0 \\ 3{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ \frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

We say that two vectors v1 and v2 are linearly independent if the only solution to the equation x1v1+x2v2=0 is x1=x2=0. Otherwise, the vectors are linearly dependent.

A set containing only two vectors is linearly dependent if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is a2=[−23−4]. To see why, notice that [−23−4]=−12[4−68]=−12a1. This way, we have 12a1−12a1=012a1+a2=0

To see why this means that a1 and a2 are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

x1a1+x2a2=0

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector That Makes a Set Linearly Dependent
content.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 8\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}-\frac{1}{2}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ \frac{1}{2}{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${x}_{2}=1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.

content.problem:
The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly dependent. Which of the following vectors could be ${a}_{2}$ if
${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

A set containing *only two* vectors is linearly *dependent* if and only if the two vectors are parallel.

From the given options, the correct answer is 

$$
{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To see why, notice that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}.
$$

This way, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} & =0 \\ \frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}-{a}_{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, the vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are parallel.

To see why this means that ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ are linearly dependent, we notice that the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0
$$

has the solution ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}$ and ${x}_{2}=-1,$ which is different from ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the set is linearly dependent.
